title: Best AI animated explainer video makers for SaaS teams (2026)
summary: Compare AI animated explainer video makers for SaaS launches and customer education. Find the right style, tool, and update workflow.
body_markdown:
## What "animated explainer video" actually covers


An animated explainer video can put fictional characters, drawn diagrams, moving graphics, or the real product on screen. Each style calls for different source material and different work when the message changes.


Character animation uses illustrated people to act out a scripted situation. You choose their actions, expressions, and camera shots, which makes the style useful for customer stories or training conversations. Whiteboard explainers draw a concept step by step, often with a hand or pen effect. They work well when a simple diagram can carry the explanation and you do not need to show the interface.


AI-generated motion graphics animate text, shapes, diagrams, and other visual elements using a prompt or existing material. You still need to check whether the sequence explains the right thing and follows your brand rules. Real-product hybrid explainers pair footage of the actual interface with animated callouts or transitions. They require a usable product flow, but viewers can see the screens they will use.


If you have a small marketing or customer education staff, you may need to revise the same explainer after several releases. For that team, the time required to replace a changed screen or correct a claim can matter as much as the time required to make the first video.

## Character animation: Vyond


Vyond is a strong pick when an explainer needs characters to act out a situation. Its character creator and scene controls let a trainer direct a scripted exchange, with text-to-speech available for narration. A SaaS education team might use it to show how a support agent handles a difficult customer conversation, while an internal trainer might use it for culture or soft-skills lessons. Vyond Go can also start a video from a prompt, document, script, or URL.


For a small team, per-user pricing and the work of maintaining the finished video deserve a closer look. Starter costs $58 per month billed annually for one user. Professional costs $100 per user per month billed annually and adds collaboration. Enterprise costs $137 per user per month billed annually. Vyond supports screen recordings and mixed media, so it can show a product alongside animation. It does not produce a matching written guide, though, so you would need to make that separately if learners need one.


## Whiteboard and doodle style: Animaker


Animaker suits a small SaaS team that wants a template-driven whiteboard explainer for a product launch or top-of-funnel campaign. Its doodle style lets you introduce a concept without building a character-led story or filming the product.


Whiteboard animation starts on the Starter plan, which costs $25 per month billed annually. Starter includes 3,000 AI video credits per month and caps videos at 15 minutes. Pro costs $43 per month billed annually, with 5,000 monthly credits and a 30-minute cap. Max costs $79 per month billed annually and raises the cap to 45 minutes. Animaker also offers a free plan, but exports carry a watermark.


A short launch explainer may fit within Starter’s 15-minute limit. If you plan to make longer onboarding videos, check the cap before choosing a plan, and account for AI credits if you expect to generate frequently.


## AI motion graphics and prompt-built explainers: Powtoon and Clueso


Powtoon suits presentation-style animated explainers built from a prompt or document. You can edit the generated video and use character or whiteboard styles. Its Free plan limits videos to three minutes and adds a watermark. Lite costs $15 per month billed yearly, includes 300 AI credits per annual renewal, and allows five watermark-free exports each month. Professional costs $40 per month billed yearly with 500 annual AI credits. Advanced costs $125 per month billed yearly with 1,200 annual AI credits and fuller character customization.


Powtoon’s AI credits renew annually, not monthly, so a small team planning frequent launches should estimate how many generations it will need across the year. Export limits also matter on Lite if you publish several videos each month.


Clueso builds branded explainers from a prompt, script, document,[deck](https://www.clueso.io/features/ppt-video) ,[PDF](https://www.clueso.io/tools/pdf-to-video-converter) , URL, or recording. Its[AI motion graphics](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) can animate product screens, logos, text, and data, and the output includes an editable video and matching written guide. Basic motion graphics are available on Free and Solo. Advanced motion graphics require Business or Enterprise.


## Real-product hybrid explainers: Clueso


Clueso is the hybrid pick when you need branded animation and the real product in the same explainer. Start with a prompt, script, document,[slide deck](https://www.clueso.io/features/ppt-video) ,[PDF](https://www.clueso.io/tools/pdf-to-video-converter) , URL, or recording. It builds an editable video with[motion graphics](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) and a matching step-by-step written guide. For a feature launch, you could animate the problem and key benefit, then show the feature in the actual interface.


Clueso gives a small team ways to keep that format consistent across releases. A brand kit carries your visual identity, and[Clueprints](https://www.clueso.io/clueprints) can carry the structure and editing style into the next video. You can adjust the script, voiceover, graphics, and clips in the editor. If the explainer depends on characters acting out a story, Vyond is the more direct fit.


Clueso also offers two ways to handle product changes. On any[plan](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) , you can re-record one changed screen and replace its clip without rebuilding the whole video. On Enterprise, a GitHub connection can flag videos affected by changes to your own product code.[Auto Updates](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-updates) , a paid Enterprise add-on, can then record the product flow again and rewrite the video and guide. Those plan gates matter if frequent feature releases make updates a regular part of the work.


## Matching the style to the job: launches vs. onboarding vs. frequent updates


A product launch needs a video that explains what changed and looks consistent with the rest of your brand. For a new analytics dashboard, a real-product hybrid explainer can show the dashboard while motion graphics call attention to the numbers customers should notice. Clueso can build that video from a prompt, deck, document, or recording, then produce a matching written guide. If the launch instead calls for characters acting out a customer problem, Vyond’s character animation is the better style.


Onboarding calls for a different choice when customers need to repeat a task. A hybrid explainer can show someone setting up an integration in the actual product, and the written guide gives customers steps to follow later. Character animation can help explain a policy or a conversation, but it adds scene-editing work when the goal is to show where a user clicks.


Frequent releases favor a format you can revise without starting over. If a settings screen changes every few weeks, Clueso lets you replace the affected clip on any plan. For feature education tied closely to the interface, test that update workflow alongside each tool’s first-draft speed.


## Buying criteria for SaaS teams


Run the same launch brief through each explainer video maker, then revise a finished video after changing one product screen. Time both tasks so you can compare first-draft effort with the work required after a release.


- **Small-team effort.** Ask one marketer or educator to make a draft without a motion designer. Time the work needed to fix narration, timing, and visuals after the first version.
- **Input flexibility.** Give each tool the material you already have, whether that is a prompt, document, deck, or recording. Check whether it builds a useful explainer from that material or leaves you to assemble the visuals.
- **Brand consistency.** Make two videos with the same fonts, colors, and layout rules. Check whether reusable templates keep them consistent and which plan gives your team access to those controls.
- **Update effort.** Change a product screen and see whether you can replace one clip, revise the narration, and update the written guide without rebuilding everything. Clueso supports clip replacement on any plan. GitHub-connected change detection requires Enterprise, while[Auto Updates](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-updates) is a paid Enterprise add-on.
- **Cost at volume.** Price your expected editors and monthly output, not one video. Check export limits, AI credits, and plan gates. Powtoon allocates AI credits annually, and Vyond charges per user. Clueso lists its seat and plan costs on its[pricing page](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) .


## FAQs


**What’s the best AI animated explainer video tool for a SaaS team?** Vyond suits scripted character stories, Animaker suits template-based whiteboard explainers, and Powtoon suits presentation-style animation. Clueso fits branded motion graphics and real-product videos that need a matching written guide and regular updates. Choose based on what viewers need to see and how often the video will change.


**How can a small team make animated explainers without a designer or animator?** Start with material you already have. Clueso can build an editable video and guide from a prompt, script, document, deck, PDF, or recording. For a doodle-style explainer, Animaker provides templates you can adapt without drawing each scene.


**How does an animated product explainer differ from a character-animation explainer?** An animated product explainer shows the interface and uses motion graphics to explain what a feature does. A character-animation explainer uses illustrated people and scenes to tell a story, such as how a customer handles a common problem. Choose the first when viewers need to recognize the product they will use.


**How can you keep explainers current through frequent feature releases?** On any Clueso plan, you can re-record a changed screen and replace that clip instead of rebuilding the video. On Enterprise, a GitHub connection can flag videos affected by changes to your product code.[Auto Updates](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-updates) , a paid Enterprise add-on, can record the flow again and revise the video and guide.


## Conclusion


Test your shortlist with one launch brief and one changed product screen. You will see which tool can make the explainer your customers need and which one your team can keep current after release.
